title: Slotted prefetch bridge to reduce CPU↔GPU sync, memory copies, and threadpool contention
creator: Asha Reddy
description:
Problem: The host-side prefill->decode pipeline still exhibits high tail CPU latency under bursty traffic primarily due to repeated small pinned-memory memcpy operations, frequent CPU↔GPU synchronization points, and threadpool contention when many concurrent requests trigger cache/prefill flows. These manifest as increased 95th and 99th CPU latencies, lower effective GPU batch sizes, and higher per-token host cost.

Goal: Implement a 'slotted prefetch bridge' — a lightweight host-side mechanism that: (1) aggregates small prefill copies into per-stream pinned staging slots to reduce memcpy ops, (2) converts many short host-GPU syncs into batched async signals to lower scheduler wakeups, (3) provides kernel-selection hints (attention tiling, kv-cache layout) to the GPU runtime ahead of execution to avoid last-moment remapping, and (4) reduces threadpool contention via a dedicated IO/transfer workerset with cooperative steal policy.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- Reduce host 95th-percentile CPU latency on prefill path by >=30% under the 'summary-burst' workload (1000 qps spikes, 256 seq).
- Reduce total host->device memcpy bytes per request on average by >=40% on sampled workloads.
- Decrease number of host wakeups per request by >=3 on average (measured via perf counters).
- Maintain or improve GPU utilization (+/-2% tolerance) and model output correctness.

Approach & design decisions:
1) Slotted staging: allocate a small fixed-size pool of per-stream pinned staging slots (configurable N slots per stream). Incoming prefill fragments are appended into slots until a slot is full or a dispatch timer fires (coalescing window). This reduces syscall/memcpy overhead and removes micro-sized DMA submissions.
2) Async fence batching: instead of immediate CPU cudaEvent synchronization after each memcpy, we issue events for the batch and use a single polling/epoll integrated waiter that completes multiple events together. This reduces expensive thread wakeups.
3) Kernel hint API: the host annotates requests with expected attention tiling and kv layout patterns (e.g., 'split-attn-tiles=32' or 'kv-format=interleaved') so the GPU runtime can pick kernels without runtime probing. These hints are advisory and fallback remains.
4) Threadpool rework: create a small dedicated transfer workerset pinned to non-NUMA CPU core(s) and use cooperative work-stealing from the general-purpose runtime threadpool. Transfer tasks are enqueued as compact descriptors to minimize queue contention.
5) Fallback & safety: if slotted staging is saturated, fall back to existing direct-copy path. Also expose per-tenant throttle and diagnostics.

Implementation plan (steps):
- Spike: prototype slotted staging with a single-slot per-stream and measure memcpy counts (2d).
- Iteration: extend to N slots, implement coalescing timer (3d).
- Integrate async fence batching and global waiter (2d).
- Add kernel-hint metadata propagation to request envelope and runtime consumer (3d).
- Threadpool workerset and cooperative stealing (3d).
- End-to-end integration tests, conformance checks, and perf runs (4d).
- Rollout: server-side feature flag, canary on low-traffic clusters, metrics dashboard updates (2d).

Risks & mitigation:
- Memory pressure from pinned slots: make slots configurable and enforce global cap + LRU eviction across streams.
- Latency regression for small single-shot requests: tune coalescing window to be small (<=250us) and bypass for latency-sensitive routes.
- Kernel hint mismatch causing suboptimal kernels: keep conservative defaults and add telemetry to detect mismatches and auto-disable hints per-model.

Telemetry & dashboards: add metrics: slots_allocated, slots_coalesced_bytes, memcpy_calls_reduced, async_waiter_wakeups, hint_mismatches, transfer_worker_queue_length. Add a perf dashboard panel comparing baseline vs canary cluster for 50/95/99 CPU latency and GPU utilization.

Notes: This ticket targets runtime-1.19 and is expected to complement ENG-33247's host coalescing work and ENG-38021's token-aware coalescer. The new kernel-hint interface will be proposed as a small schema extension to the request proto (backwards compatible).
comments: 2025-02-15 — Spike started: prototype single-slot staging. Early microbench: memcpy syscalls reduced from 9->3 per prefill request for 256-seq. Baseline CPU 95th fell ~18% in this microbench.

2025-02-18 — Design review notes from runtime team: agree on per-stream slot pool; request to add global memory cap and LRU eviction to avoid OOM. @Maya Patel suggested exposing slot backpressure metric for customer-visibility.

2025-02-22 — Implemented async fence batching prototype. Observed thread wakeups down ~4 per request in synthetic harness. Will integrate with global waiter thread that polls epoll on Linux. @Diego Vazquez to review epoll integration PR.

2025-02-26 — Kernel hint schema provisional: added 'hint.attn_tile', 'hint.kv_format', 'hint.expected_seq_len'. Telemetry to record actual kernel chosen vs hinted. Need runtime fallback logic in case of mismatch.

2025-03-01 — End-to-end perf run on canary cluster (mixed workload): host memcpy bytes per request down 44% median; host 95th CPU on prefill path down 33%; overall GPU utilization steady (+1.2%). Test vectors attached. Good signal; plan to widen canary.
2025-03-03 — PRs: split staging and waiter changes; threadpool workerset in progress. @Evan Li noted a potential regression on low-traffic p95; added route bypass for low-latency tagged requests.
